spec.hypothesis: Marketplace-ask H100 series are noisy with frequent repricing, but the medium band is too wide. Always-narrow scores 0.0560 against 0.0616 for medium, which is the largest single-series gain in the brief. I expect narrow to win on unseen origins.

Hyperscaler spot series are almost always unchanged (81-97% unchanged days, zero q80 move), but the actor's medium band is too narrow for the rare jumps. Always-wide scores 0.01122 vs 0.01206 on A100_40GB and 0.01238 vs 0.01466 on A100_SXM_80GB, and it beats drift on both. Promote wide for the hyperscaler_spot class. This is a different class from the rejected marketplace_ask edit.

Series that reprice often (under 50% unchanged days) get too much width from medium. Always-narrow beats medium on both of them: H100 marketplace ask 0.0560 vs 0.0616, and H100_80GB neocloud 0.0126 vs 0.0136. Selecting by unchanged_fraction < 0.5 covers both. It differs from the rejected marketplace_ask-only edit and uses a regime feature that should generalize better.

H100_80GB series reprice often (unchanged fraction 2-34%). Always-narrow beats medium on both: marketplace ask 0.0560 vs 0.0616 and neocloud rate card 0.0126 vs 0.0136. Selecting by gpu_model == H100_80GB covers both and differs from the rejected marketplace-only edit. It avoids the unchanged_fraction threshold that was not programmable. It leaves H100_SXM_80GB alone, where narrow loses.

A100_SXM_80GB series are mostly unchanged but have rare jumps. Always-wide cuts hyperscaler spot pinball from 0.01466 to 0.01238, a gain of 0.00228. It raises neocloud rate card pinball from 0.00676 to 0.00759, a loss of 0.00083. The net gain is positive. The class is a different set of decisions from the rejected instrument_class edits, and it mixes two instrument classes, so it is less of a single-regime bet.

A100_40GB series are mostly unchanged days with rare jumps, so medium is too narrow. Always-wide scores 0.01122 vs 0.01206 on hyperscaler spot, a gain of 0.00084. It scores 0.02663 vs 0.02614 on the neocloud rate card, a loss of 0.00049. The net gain is small but positive. This is a different decision set from the rejected instrument_class edits and from the A100_SXM_80GB edit.

Series with a non-trivial daily move (relative_q80 >= 0.001) are the H100 marketplace ask and the H100_80GB neocloud rate card. Always-narrow beats medium on both: 0.0560 vs 0.0616, and 0.0126 vs 0.0136. The flat A100 and hyperscaler series (q80 = 0) stay untouched. This is a different test from the rejected marketplace-only edit. It uses the continuous move-size feature instead of the unchanged_fraction and gpu_model tests that were not programmable.

Neocloud rate-card is the only instrument class not yet tried. Medium is already near-best on three of its four series. Narrow wins clearly on H100_80GB (0.0126 vs 0.0136) and is close to flat on A100_40GB (0.0265 vs 0.0261). The other two series lose about 0.001 each, so the net result is uncertain and may be slightly negative. I'm choosing it because instrument_class edits are the only kind the kernel has programmed so far. The remaining class either has no gain or was already rejected.

Only instrument_class edits have been programmable so far, and the marketplace_ask-narrow and hyperscaler_spot-wide edits both failed on held-out origins. Summed over the seven series, always-narrow scores 0.1544 against 0.1558 for medium and 0.1858 for wide. Narrow wins big on the two H100_80GB series. It loses about 0.0006 to 0.002 on the flat series. A single global shift is a clean decision set (all), so it should be programmable. It is the only unrejected option with a positive net expected gain, though a small one.

Series with zero daily move (relative_q80 < 0.0001) are flat with rare jumps, so medium is too narrow. Always-wide gains 0.0008 on A100_40GB spot and 0.0023 on A100_SXM_80GB spot. It loses about 0.0005 and 0.0008 on the two flat neocloud A100 series, so the net is about +0.0017. This is a move-size regime test, not an instrument_class or gpu_model test, so it selects a different set of decisions from the rejected hyperscaler-only edit.

Decisions where fewer than 10% of the last 60 days were unchanged are almost all H100 marketplace-ask origins, with a few at the high end of the range falling outside the class. Always-narrow scores 0.0560 against 0.0616 for medium on that series, and the gain should come from the origins with the most repricing. The test selects a subset of the origins in the rejected marketplace_ask edit, so it is not a duplicate. It also avoids mixing in the neocloud H100_80GB series, which made the earlier 0.5 threshold not programmable.

Decisions with unchanged_fraction < 0.3 are the H100 marketplace ask origins plus the most active H100_80GB neocloud origins. Always-narrow beats medium on both (0.0560 vs 0.0616, and 0.0126 vs 0.0136). The cutoff sits below the 0.5 test that was not programmable, so it selects a different and tighter set than any earlier proposal. It leaves the flat A100 and H100_SXM series untouched.

Origins with at least 95% unchanged days in the last 60 are the flattest stretches. They are mostly A100_40GB hyperscaler spot origins plus fully flat neocloud A100 origins. In these stretches the rare jump is not covered by the medium band. Always-wide gains 0.0008 on A100_40GB spot (0.01122 vs 0.01206). The cutoff selects a tighter, different set of decisions than the rejected instrument_class and relative_q80 < 0.0001 edits, and it avoids the lower-flatness A100_SXM and H100 origins. The neocloud A100 series lose a little under wide, so the gain is small and uncertain.

The 0.9 cutoff is looser than the 0.95 test that was not programmable, and it is a different decision set from the rejected instrument_class and relative_q80 edits.

It is a different set of decisions because the 0.1 cutoff also selects origins between 5% and 10%, so it should not be a duplicate. It avoids the H100_80GB neocloud origins that made the wider cutoffs hard to program.
